text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Norwegian papers this morning.
- Several Norwegian industrial companies are considering moving production to Iceland because of lower energy costs.

-A majority in parliament wants to increase funding to hospitals, going against the government's proposals. Opposition parties are calling for more money after several hospitals said they would have to cut doctors' working hours to reduce wage costs.
- Den norske Bank raised its bid for mortgage lender Bolig og Naeringsbanken to 196.50 crowns plus 10.50 crowns dividend for 1996 for a total of 207 crowns per share.

- Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse may be forced to sell its insurance division, Norske Liv, before it can go ahead with a proposed merger with insurer Storebrand because of its competitive position in the insurance market.
- For the first time in two years tabloid newspapers have increased their circulation.
